_readme: Relay's detection benchmark. Every case is a line of sermon speech as an ASR
system would transcribe it, plus the verses that SHOULD reach the screen.
This exists because the moat was unmeasured. docs/SPEC.md sets a target of a
<5% wrong-verse rate and nothing anywhere checked it. You cannot improve what
you have never baselined.
Run it:  cargo test eval -- --nocapture
It also runs in CI, so detection quality is a GATE and not a vibe.
THREE KINDS OF CASE, and the negatives matter most:
expect: [refs]  — these verses must be found.
expect: []      — a NEGATIVE. Nothing may fire. Most of these are real
failures pulled out of a live rehearsal: garbled speech
that made Relay put the wrong scripture on a wall.
must_not_fire   — the verse may be SUGGESTED, but must never auto-fire.
Paraphrases live here: an uncalibrated TF-IDF score is
not a probability and must never reach a congregation
without a human agreeing first.
ADDING CASES IS THE MOST USEFUL THING YOU CAN DO. Especially: real sermon
lines in Yorùbá, Kiswahili and Hausa, and real ASR mistakes. A case that
fails is not a problem — it is the point. See docs/LANGUAGES.md.
REAL SERMON LINES — `source: FIELD-2026-08-30`.
Six cases are not written by anyone. They are verbatim ASR output from a live
service (docs/audits/FIELD-2026-08-30.md), taken from `detections.heard_text` —
the column that exists because a service once put wrong verses on a wall and the
log could not say what it had heard.
Five are references the preacher really made and Relay really caught. Four of
those five are the bare "Deuteronomy 15, 7" shape that this codebase demotes on
purpose, over the standing objection that nobody speaks that way. This preacher
did, four times in thirty minutes. DO NOT TIGHTEN THAT DEMOTION WITHOUT READING
THIS PARAGRAPH.
The sixth is the one that went wrong: the preacher cited Luke 10:32-37 and Relay
put Proverbs 3:32 on the wall, because a passage fired by hand half an hour
earlier was still what a bare verse number attached to. It is a NEGATIVE — nothing
may fire from it. Getting Luke 10 onto the wall would be a fine outcome and is not
required; putting up a verse nobody said is the defect.
AND WHAT THIS CORPUS CANNOT SEE, SAID HERE RATHER THAN ASSUMED.
The scorer drives `detect_direct` and the real router. It does NOT drive
`ContextMemory`, so a case cannot exercise a bare verse number resolved against
a passage fired earlier — which is exactly how the Luke 10 line went wrong.
That negative guards the PARSER against producing Proverbs from those words; the
context path it actually failed on is guarded in `detection.rs`
(`field_a_bare_verse_belongs_to_the_book_this_sentence_names`) and in `main.rs`.
A green scorecard is not evidence about the context path.
ORDINARY PREACHING THAT USED TO FIRE — `source: R4-audit`.
Eleven negatives that are not garble and not edge cases. They are plain sermon
sentences, and every one of them put a verse on a wall before the
`UncertainNumber` repair: "Nehemiah, fifty two days they built the wall" became
Nehemiah 5:2 at 0.77, "romans eight one two" became Romans 8:1, and at the TOP of
the sensitivity dial every deliberate demotion in detection.rs was inert.
They are here rather than only in detection.rs because the dial sweep
(`r4_04`) scores this corpus at six positions from 0 to 100 — so these are what
makes that sweep bite. Without them it passed with the repair removed.

cases.note: A quoted paraphrase. May be SUGGESTED, must never auto-fire — a TF-IDF cosine is not a probability.

cases.note: 'Iṣẹ́' means 'work'. If it were an alias for Acts, this would fire scripture off normal speech.

cases.text: Ẹ jẹ́ ká kọ orin 3 pẹ̀lú ayọ̀
cases.note: 'Orin' means 'song'. In a church. Must never be an alias for Song of Solomon.

cases.text: Yohana sura ya tatu, mstari wa kumi na sita
cases.note: Fully in-language: 'chapter three, verse sixteen'. kumi na sita = 10+6.

cases.text: Zaburi sura ya ishirini na tatu, mstari wa kwanza
cases.note: ishirini na tatu = 23. 'kwanza' is the ORDINAL 'first' — how a verse is actually said.

cases.text: Warumi sura ya nane, aya ya ishirini na nane
Zaburi sura ya mia moja na kumi na tatu, mstari wa kwanza
cases.note: THE TRAP. 'mia moja' = 100 (hundred-one), NOT 101. The multiplier comes AFTER.

cases.text: Zaburi sura ya mia mbili, mstari wa kwanza
cases.note: 'mia mbili' = 200. The English parser would have read 100+2 = 102 and shown the wrong psalm.

cases.text: Yahaya sura ta uku, aya ta goma sha shida
cases.note: goma sha shida = 10 sha 6 = 16.

cases.text: Zabura sura ta ashirin da uku, aya ta farko
cases.note: ashirin da uku = 23. 'farko' = first.

cases.text: Zabura sura ta dari da goma sha uku, aya ta farko
cases.note: dari da goma sha uku = 100 + 13.

cases.text: Zabura sura ta dari biyu, aya ta farko
cases.note: 'dari biyu' = 200, not 102. Multiplier after the hundred word.

cases.text: Yahaya sura ta huɗu, aya ta ɗaya
cases.note: Hooked ɗ folds to d — ɗaya = 1.

cases.text: Tunashukuru Mungu na familia yetu ya kanisa
cases.note: 'na' and 'ya' are everywhere in Swahili. They must never manufacture a reference.

cases.text: Muna godiya ga Allah da iyalinmu na coci
cases.note: 'da' and 'na' are everywhere in Hausa.

cases.text: Please turn to hymn number three sixteen.
cases.note: THE 2026-08-14 P0. 'number' is one edit from the book 'numbers', and the fuzzy gate ('the next token is a number') is exactly the shape of an announcement. This put Numbers 3:16 on a wall at 0.840 against a 0.50 bar. The Yoruba twin (neg-yo-everyday-song) was already here; the English one never was, which is how a corpus can see a trap and still miss it.

cases.text: The youth meet in room two twelve after the service.
cases.note: 'room' is one edit from the typing shortcut 'rom' -> Romans 2:12. The abbreviation table was built for typing and was being used for listening.

cases.text: There are free seats on row three sixteen.
cases.note: 'row' -> 'rom' -> Romans. Same single edit, different everyday word.

cases.text: We will sing song two twelve this morning.
cases.note: The English twin of neg-yo-everyday-song. An EXACT alias, not a repair: 'song' is an ordinary word AND a book name, so it now needs a chapter/verse keyword to auto-fire.

cases.text: He fasted for day three sixteen of the challenge.
cases.note: 'day' and 'van' are one edit from 'dan' -> Daniel.

cases.text: Let us read Psalm three sixteen together.
cases.note: The CONTROL for the negatives above. 'Psalm' is not an everyday noun colliding with a book, it is how every preacher names the book, and it must keep auto-firing. A safety fix that breaks this row has overshot.

cases.text: Song of Solomon chapter two verse twelve.
cases.note: The other control: an ordinary-word book name WITH explicit reference language is unambiguous and still auto-fires.
